findings.title: Null guard applied only to getSubGroupsCount; other getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE
findings.body: The fix makes getSubGroupsCount() tolerate modelSupplier.get() returning null (group deleted concurrently), but getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 all still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. The same concurrent delete/read scenario (issue #40368) will still throw a NullPointerException through these code paths, e.g. when a group listing is served with pagination or search while the group is being deleted. The fix should be applied consistently (delegate to an empty stream, or the cached subgroups set, when the underlying model is gone).

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined; test is racy and can hang indefinitely
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background reader thread is started but never joined: the test sets deletedAll=true and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. If the thread has not yet observed the flag, or is in the middle of a request that fails, the final assertion can run before the exception is recorded, producing a flaky false-pass. Additionally, the while(!deletedAll.get()) loop has no iteration cap or timeout, so if a single admin call blocks (e.g. server-side deadlock), the test hangs forever instead of failing. Use a CountDownLatch/ExecutorService with awaitTermination(timeout) and join the thread before asserting.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount can now return null, changing the method contract
findings.body: Previously getSubGroupsCount() either returned a Long from the delegate or threw (NPE). Now it can return null when the group was deleted concurrently. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount blindly call representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount()), so a deleted group's representation will serialize subGroupCount: null instead of throwing or being treated as deleted. If returning null is the intended semantic for 'group no longer exists', callers and the REST layer should handle it; otherwise prefer 0L or skip the group.
